title: canary-failure-rootcause-scrapbook
body:
Context:
- Quick brain dump after a rough canary this morning. Personal scratchpad for steps tried, observations, and next actions. Not a runbook yet.

Timeline / high-level:
- 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC: Canary deploy started (pipeline #872). Canary subset = 3% traffic to cluster region-us-west2.
- 03:25 UTC: Error spike: 5xx rate from canary pods rose from 0.7% -> 6.8% over ~5 min window. Latency P95 doubled.
- 03:32 UTC: Autoscaler for canary group added 2 pods, but errors persisted.
- 03:40 UTC: We attempted a fast revert by pinning traffic back to stable (see commands below) but rollback didn't fully reduce errors — some stable traffic still impacted.

What I saw (raw):
- Pod logs (canary): several exceptions: "KVCacheMiss: unexpected null for key" coming from runtime client, stack shows model-serving-layer -> token-cache -> transport layer.
- Error sample from app logs:
  ERROR 2026-03-09T03:26:12Z service.go:142 "handler panic" trace="runtime.go:..." msg="KVCacheMiss: unexpected null for key user:session:abc123"
- Kube events: OOMKilled reported for 1 canary pod at 03:27 UTC, memory footprint spiked to ~3.2GB vs usual 1.1GB for same model/seqLen.
- Downstream: small correlation with Redis latency jump (client observed 200ms -> 1.2s) around same time, but not all errors reference cache lookup.

Artifacts / versions involved:
- Canary image: gcr.io/redwood/canary-inference:2026-03-09-7f3a2b (image digest sha256:aa3f4d...).
- Stable image: gcr.io/redwood/inference:2026-02-26-9d1c8f (sha256:9b2c7e...).
- Model variant: v2-quant-8bit (on canary) vs v2-quant-8bit (stable) — same model, but runtime flags differ (canary had KV_CACHE=true, BATCHER=adaptive).
- Helm chart: release/producer v1.14.2 (no change from previous), but rollout controller logs show "featureFlag.kvEviction=experimental" enabled for canary label.

Commands I ran (copied from terminal):
- routed 100% back to stable (quick):
  # kubectl patch svc inference-route -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"canary":"false"}}}'
  -> svc updated, but ingress LB had cached routes for ~30s, verified using curl -I X-Canary header

- manual scale down
  kubectl scale deployment/inference-canary --replicas=0 -n prod
  -> terminated canary pods, but a few requests still hitting canary pods (stale endpoints in envoy), I ran envoy admin /clusters refresh on each node.

- garbage collection / purge local caches on redis client used by runtime:
  redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 BGREWRITEAOF
  redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 INFO memory
  -> memory high but not exhausted; no major evictions logged.

- inspected node metrics where OOM occurred:
  ssh into node node-usw2-45, checked dmesg -> saw OOM killer: PID 12345 (inference-process) killed after allocation failure.

Immediate hypotheses (ordered by likelihood in my head):
1) Canary runtime flags enabled KV_CACHE and experimental eviction algorithm -> caused memory leak under specific request shape (long sequences), leading to OOM and mid-request failures -> 5xx.
2) Indirect cascade: Redis latency spike caused runtime to retry/block, increasing memory pressure and KV cache growth -> OOM.
3) Model change? (unlikely, model artifact same tag) but maybe quantization path takes more transient memory in combination with BATCHER=adaptive -> larger batch windows -> memory spike.
4) Envoy routing stale endpoints caused some requests to hit half-dead pods -> 502 + 5xx noise, but doesn't explain memory usage.

Why rollback didn't fix everything immediately:
- Envoy/ingress caches endpoints for 20-30s; some nodes still had endpoints in warm pool.
- A few canary pods got into a crashloop and left partial state in Redis (locks) causing subsequent requests to block on slow redis ops.
- The autoscaler had created extra canary pods that inherited experimental flag; when we scaled down, some nodes continued to replay queued work (work-queue persisted to disk?) -> not fully sure.

Next immediate actions (short):
- Reproduce locally with high seqLen synthetic traffic and KV_CACHE enabled, reproduce memory growth trace. (Link: repro harness on my laptop: ./tools/repro/canary_kv_leak.sh)
- Disable featureFlag.kvEviction for rollout controller and rerun canary with controlled traffic (1% -> monitor for 30m).
- Patch runtime to add more logging around KV cache insert/size; deploy to staging and run load test.

Longer-term / follow-ups:
- Add a canary-gating step in CI: any runtime flag changes that touch cache/eviction require staging load test with long sequence traces.
- Add a kill-switch annotation to quickly force all nodes to refresh envoy config (or use service annotation to reduce TTL).
- Investigate if adaptive batcher increases transient memory beyond node resource limits; update resource requests to account for worst-case.

Quick checklist for postmortem entry (things to capture):
- exact image digests, runtime flag diffs, helm values diff (can get from release tags).
- timeline of autoscaler rep count, OOM events (kube node dmesg), envoy route cache delays.
- correlation graph of redis latency vs 5xx rate (30s bins).
- snippet of failing stacktrace + approximate line numbers for devs.

Notes-to-self:
- When doing fast revert next time: 1) drain canary pods from LB first (kubectl annotate svc ingress-proxy refresh=true) -> wait 45s -> scale down; 2) run envoy cluster refresh; 3) then heal redis if needed.
- Document the reproducer script path and make it executable for on-call.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Why did one node see memory spike while others didn't? Need to check request affinity / sticky sessions.
- Did the canary get a different config from central config store? (check configmap revision used in canary pods)
- Are there pending PRs that flip kvEviction flag? (cross-check linked PRs).

Scratch CLI snippets I want to save (for replay):
- get pod logs between times:
  kubectl logs -n prod inference-canary-7f3a2b --since=30m | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/canary-logs.txt
- collect stack traces if available:
  curl http://inference-canary-7f3a2b.prod:6060/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2 > /tmp/gors.txt
- quick heap dump (if process alive):
  kill -SIGUSR1 <pid> && scp node:/var/log/heapdump-*.prof ~/heapdumps/

Final quick mind-map (one liner):
- Probable: experimental KV eviction + adaptive batcher -> memory amplification on long seqLen -> OOM -> request failures; Redis latency likely amplified effect.

If anyone else reading: ping Marco/Jen if you see anything off in CI or the linked PR. Will convert to a proper incident timeline and postmortem after reproducer verified.

-- Aisha
